4. On the basis of the pleadings on 05.09.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 13.04.2023 at about 9.15 a.m., on S.C. Road,

On 09.02.2024 respondent produced the evidence of driver of the bus as RW1.
6.
On 01.03.2024 learned advocate for petitioner filed notes of arguments.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf both the parties and perused the records.

7. On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 ... In the affirmative  Issue No.2 ...

sentences.text: 2  8. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 13.04.2023 at about 09.15 a.m. when riding the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-HF-3159 on S.C. road, Sheshadripuram, near Kino junction Railway under bridge, the driver of BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2412 drove the same negligently and dashed to the motorcycle thereby caused accident, caused injuries.
9. In the written statement , respondent denied the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident.
10. In the cross-examination, petitioner stated that there was a distance of 3 feet in between left side footpath of the road and motorcycle earlier to the accident.

The petitioner denied the suggestion that on the day of accident he ride the motorcycle in the middle of the road and petitioner stated that earlier to the accident noticed the bus at the distance of 250 feet and when accident took placed bus was under the bridge.

The petitioner denied the suggestion that he dashed the motorcycle to the right side bumper of the bus due to his negligence the accident taken place and accident was not due to the negligence of the BMTC bus driver.
10 (a) In the evidence of PW.2 - Dr. Nagaraj B.N. stated nothing about the reason and mode of accident.

11. In the evidence affidavit RW1, the driver of the bus stated that he drove the bus near Kino junction railway bridge, Bengaluru on the left side of the road, the rider of the motorcycle came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner wrong side and dashed to the right front corner portion of the bus, fell on the road and suffered injuries.
In the cross-examination of RW.1 denied the suggestion that in order to reach the schedule within time, drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner.
RW.1 admitted non filing of counter complaint about the accident to the police.
RW.1 also admitted that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against him alleging that he has caused the accident.

12. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.48/2023 registered by High Grounds Traffic police against the driver of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2412 for the offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC and under Sec.134(a& b), 187 of MV Act, on the basis of the statement of Shahid Khan S/o. Azhar Khan, the petitioner.

In Ex.P.3 is the copy of sketch of the place of accident collision taken place on the eastern part of the North-South road is mentioned,
Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar recorded on 13.04.2023, Ex.P.5 is the copy of the wound certificate.

Ex.P6 is the copy the motor vehicle accident report in which motor vehicle inspector noted damage noticed in the front part of the bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2412 and motorcycle bearing No.KA- 01-HF-3159 on 15.04.2023 are mentioned, Ex.P.7 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by the High Grounds Traffic Police in Crime No.48/2023 against RW.1 driver of the bus for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and under Sec.134(a&b), 187 of IMV Act.
14.
In this case at this stage there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded on 13.04.2023 at about 9.15 p.m. when petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-HF- 3159 on S.C. road,

3

Sheshadripuram, near Kino junction Railway under bridge, RW.1- the driver of BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-2412 drove the same negligently and dashed to the motorcycle thereby caused accident,
caused injuries.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered right leg compound fracture type II with right superior and inferior pubic ramus fracture, taken treatment at Srinivas Hospital, Bengaluru, then admitted to Sparsh hospital as an inpatient and underwent surgery, then took follow up treatment by spending Rs.3,68,204/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.48,000/p.m. by working as an Operation Theatre Assistant and Part time Optometrist at Chethana Eye Care Centre, Nagavara, Bengaluru.
In the written statement respondent denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
In the cross-examination petitioner stated that he took treatment for 2 time as inpatient only 2 days.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that as on the date of evidence he has no difficulties to perform the day today activities.

PW.1 admitted that as per Ex.P.11 no amount is deducted towards ESI, PF,
income tax or other charges.
PW.1 admitted as per Ex.P.11 and 12 he was working as Optomertist (part time) & OT Assistant for the salary of Rs.28,000/- per month.
PW.1 submitted inability to produce bank account statement.

15. In the evidence of PW.2 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. stated that on 13.01.2024 on clinical examination noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 42% to right lower limb and 14% to the whole body.
In the cross- examination PW2 stated that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified the case sheet.
PW.2 submitted that fractures suffered by petitioner are united and implant are situated.
PW.2 denied the suggestion that only after removal of implants the disability can be assessed.
17. In the evidence RW1, stated nothing regarding the nature of injuries, and consequence of the treatment taken by the petitioner.

18. The wound certificate, discharge summary, medial bills shows that in the accident the petitioner has suffered right leg both bone fracture, took first aid at Srinivasa Hospital, Balepet, then took treatment at Sparsh hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 13.04.2023 to 14.04.2023 and from 01.05.2023 to 03.05.2023 by spending Rs.3,14,219/-.

In Ex.P.11 it is noticed that he was working at Chethana Eye Care Center for Rs.28,000/- to the petitioner who worked as Optomertrist (part time)
OT Assistant.
In the file there are no evidence regarding loss of income or decreasing the income of the petitioner subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I am of the opinion oral evidence of PW.2 and disability certificate issued by the PW.2 who has not treated the petitioner is not sufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income or permanent physical disability.
Hence I award compensation Rs.1,10,000/- towards Pain and sufferings, Rs.3,14,219/- towards treatment charges, Rs.15,000/- towards attendant , conveyance and nourishment charges,
Rs.1,25,000/- towards loss of income (Rs.25,000/- p.m. x5), Rs.80,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.

Shahid Khan vs B.M.T.C on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186818860/
4 20.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.6,44,219/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
19. Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondent is liable to pay Rs.6,44,219/- with current and future interest 6% p.a. to the petitioner as compensation .
Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER The application filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.
The respondent owner of BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57- F-2412 shall pay Rs.6,44,219/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount with interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 14th August , 2024)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
